Terms of Reference for the Horizon Scandal Inquiry:

1. The inquiry will establish the facts about what happened at the Post Office and to subpostmasters, including:
a. Understanding and acknowledging what went wrong and key lessons that must be learned.
b. Obtaining all available relevant evidence from the Post Office, Fujitsu, BEIS and other relevant organizations.
2. The inquiry will consider the following matters:
a. The treatment of subpostmasters, including the handling of complaints and the provision of support.
b. The role of the Post Office in the scandal, including its response to concerns raised by subpostmasters and the effectiveness of its internal controls and processes.
c. The role of Fujitsu in the development and maintenance of the Horizon system, including its response to concerns raised by subpostmasters.
d. The role of BEIS in overseeing the Post Office and its response to concerns raised about the Horizon system.
e. The effectiveness of the criminal justice system in dealing with cases related to the Horizon scandal.
3. The inquiry will make recommendations to ensure that a scandal like this cannot happen again, including:
a. The Horizon Compensation Advisory Board (HCAB) should not be prevented from monitoring individual cases.
b. HCAB shall produce written reports in respect of each of their meetings.
c. Membership of HCAB should be increased to ensure that it has sufficient capacity.
d. The government should within 28 days seek directions under section 5 of the Inquiries Act 2005 to enable the inquiry to compel the production of documents and witnesses.
4. The inquiry will operate under the Inquiries Act 2005 and will be independent of the government.
5. The inquiry will aim to produce an interim report within 6 months of its establishment and a final report within 12 months.
6. The inquiry will be chaired by a person appointed by the Secretary of State for BEIS, who will have the necessary experience and expertise to lead the inquiry effectively.
7. The inquiry will have the power to appoint assessors, experts and counsel to assist it in its work.
8. The inquiry will hold hearings in public, unless there
